newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unemployment jumps to record high.
newsitem.headline: French unemployment jumps to record high.

text.p: The number of people out of work in France hit a record high in August of 12.6 percent, official figures released on Friday showed.

The Labour Ministry figures showed the number of people unemployed in August, adjusted for seasonal variations, rose 39,500 to 3,085,100. The jobless rate, based on International Labour Organisation (ILO) criteria, which exclude jobseekers who did any work, hit a record 12.6 percent, up from 12.5 percent.
Unemployment had fallen in July by 20,000 but economists had called the drop an aberration due to seasonal factors and predicted it would rise in face of continued sluggish economic conditions.

The longer jobless lines were bad news for Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government which has made tackling unemployment one of its top priorities. Juppe has called a confidence vote in Parliament on the government's economic policy for Tuesday.
But the government received some cheer on the export front with preliminary figures showing France's trade surplus had jumped to 11.10 billion francs from a revised surplus of 9.78 billion in June.
The customs office had originally reported a surplus in June of 9.75 billion francs.
